newsitem.title: USA: US retailers probed on debt collection complaints.
newsitem.headline: US retailers probed on debt collection complaints.

text.p: Some 25 states are looking into consumer complaints about companies which surfaced following press reports of Sears, Roebuck and Co's allegedly fraudulent debt collection practices, officials said Wednesday.

Twenty-five states, the U.S. Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission held a telephone conference call Tuesday afternoon to discuss coordinating efforts to investigate Sears and other firms, Chris Barry-Smith, an assistant attorney general in Massachusetts, said Wednesday.
"Massachusetts and the other states have expressed an interest in determining whether there might be other companies engaging in this conduct," Barry-Smith told Reuters.

As a matter of company policy, Sears misled many of its once-bankrupt credit card holders into believing they had to repay their debts to the company, even though those debts were nullified by a bankruptcy court, court papers alleged.

On April 16, the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Boston ordered Sears to stop the practice in Massachusetts, where the tactic was used on more than 2,700 customers during a two-year period ending January, 1997.
A U.S. District Court judge ordered Sears on Monday to halt the allegedly "fraudulent" activities nationwide, which the massive retailer agreed to do.
The U.S. Attorney's office in Massachusetts is also seeking civil penalties, as well as restitution for debtors victimized by the practice.
"Consumer complaints are just starting to surface about other companies since the Sears matter was in the press," Barry-Smith said. "We have no idea how common it might be."

Filene's, a New England department store chain, was hit with a class-action lawsuit filed by two individuals who alleged that the Massachusetts-based retailer engaged in the same practices as Sears, the Boston Globe reported Wednesday.
St. Louis-based May Department Stores, which owns Filene's, did not return phone calls seeking comment.
